messages:
ari: hey folks, new hire here. first build for my onboarding PR fails immediately in Buildkite but GH Actions for the fork is green. I'm seeing a mix of auth errors and a git submodule SSH failure. any quick hints?

chao: welcome! paste the Buildkite log and say if you're on Windows, mac, or Linux.

ari: Windows laptop (WSL2). Buildkite job log shows two things: 
1) Submodule clone error: 
```
Cloning into 'third_party/tools'...
ssh: Could not resolve hostname github.com: Temporary failure in name resolution
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
```
2) Agent error immediately before: 
```
2026-04-02T09:12:03Z ERROR webhook: 403 Forbidden - app does not have Deployments scope
```

chao: ok two independent fixes. For the submodule SSH/WSL DNS issue, sometimes company DNS not reachable from WSL until you enable Windows host DNS passthrough. Quick workaround: in WSL run `sudo sh -c "echo 'nameserver 8.8.8.8' > /etc/resolv.conf"` then retry git clone. But long-term we prefer using HTTPS submodule URLs for onboarding or ensure your SSH agent is forwarding keys. Did you add your SSH key to your GitHub account?

ari: i did add SSH key to GitHub, but the CI job runs on Buildkite workers which clone the repo server-side, so it's failing there, not locally. the pipeline uses a deploy SSH key stored in Buildkite env var SUBMODULE_SSH_KEY. maybe that secret is empty?

chao: good catch. Check project/env vars in Buildkite web UI. If SUBMODULE_SSH_KEY is missing or the variable was redacted after a token rotation, the worker won't have the key and server-side git over SSH will fail.

devops-bot: Tip: to debug submodule SSH auth, enable DEBUG_GIT=true in the pipeline step and re-run to see the expanded git command. Also check pipeline env vars at https://buildkite.com/redwood/onboarding/pipelines/ssh-submodules/settings/env

ari: i checked and SUBMODULE_SSH_KEY is present but empty string (looks like someone removed it during secret cleanup).

chao: we'll re-add it. Also the webhook 403 about Deployments scope means the Redwood CI GitHub App currently lacks Deployments permission for that repo. That prevents Buildkite from creating deployment statuses. Do you have org admin to reconfigure the app?

ari: no org admin. can infra add the Deployments scope?

infra-bot: Action requested: Add 'Deployments' permission to GitHub App 'Redwood CI' for repo 'onboarding/ssh-sandbox' by @chao. Approvers: @ops-leads. Ticket: https://tickets.redwood.com/CI-4002

chao: while infra handles the app perms, i'll re-populate the SUBMODULE_SSH_KEY in the Buildkite pipeline from the vault copy. Ari, after that you may need to re-run the build.

buildkite-bot: Buildkite build #88 failed: job 'ci:checkout' exited 1. Logs: https://buildkite.com/redwood/onboarding/88/jobs/2

ari: thanks. quick Q: where do I get the vault copy? i'm new and don't have vault UI perms.

chao: infra will push the secret for onboarding. infra usually drops onboarding-only secrets into the Buildkite project with a note. If you need to inspect, ask #eng-infra and infra can confirm.

infra-bot: Notice: SUBMODULE_SSH_KEY injected into pipeline 'onboarding/ssh-submodules' by @chao.

chao: perms for the GH App updated to include Deployments. infra confirmed SAML/SSO approved if needed.

infra-bot: Action complete: GitHub App 'Redwood CI' granted Deployments scope for 'onboarding/ssh-sandbox' by @ops-leads.

ari: rebuild triggered. also FYI the onboarding doc mentions Windows-specific WSL DNS tweaks; can we add a note about server-side submodule SSH keys too?

buildkite-bot: Buildkite build #89 started: https://buildkite.com/redwood/onboarding/89

ari: build now gets past clone but fails later complaining agent token invalid: 
```
ERR: buildkite-agent: register: 401 Unauthorized - token revoked
```

chao: that means the Buildkite agent token used by the worker is revoked. For self-hosted agents, the token sits in the agent config or k8s secret. If this is an infra-managed worker pool, infra rotated the token and didn't roll the worker yet. I'll escalate.

infra-bot: Incident: Agent token rotation impacted onboarding pool 'onboard-windows'. Assigned to @ops-leads. See https://ops.redwood.com/incidents/CI-rot-23

chao: we usually do a rolling restart after token rotation. For on-prem Windows agents you need to update `C:\ProgramData\buildkite-agent\buildkite-agent.cfg` with the new token and restart the 'buildkite-agent' service. For k8s update the secret and rollout restart the deployment.

ari: i'm on a cloud worker pool, not my laptop. will wait for infra. any ETA?

infra-bot: ETA: token rollout for pool 'onboard-windows' in 15 minutes by @ops-leads. Will post when complete.

buildkite-bot: Buildkite build #89 retried and now running jobs.

ari: everything passed! :tada: thank you all. couple of follow-ups: 1) can we add a short checklist to onboarding for submodule SSH vs HTTPS and where SUBMODULE_SSH_KEY lives? 2) who to ping if agent tokens or GH App scopes change mid-onboarding?

chao: yes please open a docs PR for the checklist and tag 'ci-onboarding'. For immediate issues ping #eng-infra and tag @ops-leads; infra-bot will auto-file a ticket if a rotation affects pipelines. Welcome aboard! :wave:
